title: Multi-purpose River Projects in Africa
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 9 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Facts (to confirm): Aswan High Dam (Nile, Egypt), Kariba (Zambezi), Akosombo (Volta, Ghana), Seven Forks on the Tana (Masinga, Kamburu, Gitaru, Kindaruma, Kiambere).

skills.key_step: The child names multi-purpose river projects in Africa, their uses and their challenges.

floor.question: Which river flows north to the Mediterranean?

representations: a map of Africa with dams

board.do: Write the river for each and two uses.

misconceptions.ask: On which river is the Aswan High Dam?
misconceptions.repair: Pair each dam with its river and country on the map.

misconceptions.ask: Which is a use of a multi-purpose dam?
misconceptions.repair: List what a dam is built to give: power, irrigation, water, flood control, fish.

misconceptions.ask: Which is a challenge of a big dam?
misconceptions.repair: Sort dam facts into benefits and challenges.

misconceptions.ask: Why is Aswan called a multi-purpose project?
misconceptions.repair: Break the word: multi = many purposes.

checks.question: On which river is the Aswan High Dam?
Give one challenge of a big dam.
checks.answer: any of: high cost, displaced people, silting, water weeds, loss of land

skills.key_step: The child outlines the conditions that favoured the Tana River projects and pairs river project challenges with solutions.

floor.prerequisite: Names river projects and their challenges.
floor.question: Give one challenge of a dam.

steps: Name the river conditions: permanent, large volume, falls and gorges.
Name the land conditions: hard rock, few people.
Name the need: power and irrigation.

board.do: Draw a river dropping through a narrow gorge.

board.say: Why is this a good dam site?

board.do: Wait for "narrow, hard rock, water falls".
Write two more conditions and two solutions.

misconceptions.ask: Which site suits a dam on the Tana: a deep gorge or a flat plain?
misconceptions.repair: Model water held by a narrow gorge and spreading on a plain.

misconceptions.ask: Why was the Tana chosen for the Seven Forks dams?
misconceptions.repair: Compare the Tana with a river that dries up.

misconceptions.ask: Which solution fits silting of a dam?
misconceptions.repair: Trace the silt back to bare hills upstream.

misconceptions.ask: People must move for a new dam. What is fair?
misconceptions.repair: Read a story of families moved without help.

checks.question: Give two conditions that led to dams on the Tana.
checks.answer: any two of: permanent river, large volume, falls and gorges, hard rock, few people to displace, demand for power and irrigation

checks.question: Which solution fits silting?
checks.answer: planting trees and controlling soil erosion in the catchment
